name: Valhalla Siege
description: Ivar the Boneless is a great leader. He is trying to capture Kattegat from Lagertha. The war has begun and wave after wave Ivar's warriors are falling in battle. Ivar has $$$n$$$ warriors, he places them on a straight line in front of the main gate, in a way that the $$$i$$$-th warrior stands right after $$$(i-1)$$$-th warrior. The first warrior leads the attack. Each attacker can take up to $$$a_i$$$ arrows before he falls to the ground, where $$$a_i$$$ is the $$$i$$$-th warrior's strength. Lagertha orders her warriors to shoot $$$k_i$$$ arrows during the $$$i$$$-th minute, the arrows one by one hit the first still standing warrior. After all Ivar's warriors fall and all the currently flying arrows fly by, Thor smashes his hammer and all Ivar's warriors get their previous strengths back and stand up to fight again. In other words, if all warriors die in minute $$$t$$$, they will all be standing to fight at the end of minute $$$t$$$. The battle will last for $$$q$$$ minutes, after each minute you should tell Ivar what is the number of his standing warriors.
input_specification: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$q$$$ ($$$1 \le n, q \leq 200\,000$$$) — the number of warriors and the number of minutes in the battle. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \leq a_i \leq 10^9$$$) that represent the warriors' strengths. The third line contains $$$q$$$ integers $$$k_1, k_2, \ldots, k_q$$$ ($$$1 \leq k_i \leq 10^{14}$$$), the $$$i$$$-th of them represents Lagertha's order at the $$$i$$$-th minute: $$$k_i$$$ arrows will attack the warriors.
output_specification: Output $$$q$$$ lines, the $$$i$$$-th of them is the number of standing warriors after the $$$i$$$-th minute.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 975C — Valhalla Siege [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
